figures.caption: Figure 1:  Pooling amplification in a pixel world model. Median  log ⁡ E \log E  over test episodes at the larger effect size as frames grow from  64 64  to  4096 4096  pixels, without shared noise (A), with a frame-wide additive offset (B) and with a multiplicative gain on the blob (C). The pooled, Kish-tempered and contrast-tempered statistics are averages over the two learned models; the oracles use the true dynamics with independence pooling or with the exact joint likelihood. In A and C the Kish factor is close to one and the Kish-tempered curve coincides with the pooled one; the two oracle curves nearly coincide in every panel. Dotted line:  log ⁡ 20 \log 20 , the rejection threshold. Symmetric-log axis, linear for  | log ⁡ E | ≤ 10 |\log E|\leq 10 .
Table 1:  Statistics used in this paper. “Label” is the name in the registered and protocol documents; the paper uses the names in the first column.

Figure 2:  Diagnosis and repair on ERK-like synthetic data. (A) Median  log ⁡ E \log E  of the pooled score and of the three repair candidates in the twelve alternative cells of the selection grid; the shaded cell is the one the selection script designated hardest (§ 6.2 ). The Kish-tempered and field-mean curves nearly coincide. The pooled score fails everywhere except without shared noise under the simple generator. (B) Rejection counts before and after the field-pooling step, for the oracle predictor in four cells, and for the pipeline under the null on ERK and CcaS commands. Error bars:  95 % 95\%  Clopper–Pearson intervals. Symmetric-log axis in A.

Figure 3:  Two design effects. The Kish design effect from the median pairwise residual correlation ( x x ) against the design effect along the action contrast ( y y ), for every learned-model cell of the pixel main grid (colour: shared noise; shape: model), every oracle cell (grey crosses), and the pooled ERK training diagnostic (stars; four models and two horizons, at the diagnostic’s cell counts). Without shared noise or with gain noise, residual correlations are near zero and the Kish factor misses the correlation along the contrast (points above the diagonal); a frame-wide offset correlates the residuals but is orthogonal to the contrast (points below). The ERK points lie slightly below the diagonal, so Kish tempering is somewhat conservative there. Oracle residuals are independent pixel noise, so their contrast design effect is close to one.

Figure 4:  The stand-in trap. (A) Pixel world whose logging policy depends on the blob’s position six steps earlier, which the models do not see; no action has any effect. For each cell (shared noise and number of training episodes;  64 64  test episodes), the highest effect-report rate among the three replacement diagnostics for each learned model, and the contrast-tempered randomization test with the design-law resampler, which conditions on the full logged state, and with a resampler that draws actions from their marginal frequencies (post hoc, § 7.2 ). (B) Development stand-in construction with  512 512  units ( 256 256  replicates), for each reference model: the three replacement diagnostics, the exact and Monte Carlo e-value tests with the design law, and a randomization test with a marginal resampler. Error bars:  95 % 95\%  Clopper–Pearson intervals. Dotted line:  α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 .
Table 2:  M4 primary results (pooled statistic, registered analysis). Natural-log e-values; reject iff  E ≥ 100 E\geq 100 .

Figure 5:  The ERK evidence chain. Four-model  log ⁡ E \log E  of the registered pooled statistic in M4 (nine test fields), and of the Kish-tempered statistic in the exploratory analysis X (the same fields) and in the confirmatory test M5 (one unopened field; thirty minutes descriptive only). Horizontal bars mark the exact-form design bound of each analysis (Proposition  4 ), a command-only comparator for these Monte Carlo e-values; dashed and dotted lines mark the rejection thresholds of M4 ( E ≥ 100 E\geq 100 ) and M5 ( E ≥ 20 E\geq 20 ). Symmetric-log axis.
